boundary: These links are reader cues, not a new taxonomy, required order, or substitute for the scientific decision on each page.

links.title: Build or modify the computational model
links.note: Turn the identified source structure into the cell, composition, boundary model, and constraints you will actually calculate.

links.title: Inspect the full Brillouin zone
links.note: Use the trusted reference state as the parent of dense full-zone sampling when the claim depends on states at the Fermi level or extrema away from a chosen path.

links.title: Calculate the density of states
links.note: Reuse the same reference state for energy-resolved or projected-state analysis, then converge the sampling and broadening for that observable.

links.title: Compare with the density of states
links.note: DOS can test whether states occur near the Fermi level, but a high-symmetry band path alone does not establish their full-zone location or absence.

links.title: Inspect the full Brillouin zone
links.note: DOS near the Fermi level does not locate pockets or extrema; use dense full-zone evidence rather than inferring them from a selected band path.

links.title: Diagnose imaginary phonon frequencies
links.note: Before retrying, preserve the exact structure, electronic thresholds, q mesh or supercell, raw frequencies and eigenvectors, and code version. An imaginary mode can be physical or numerical.

links.title: SCF does not converge
links.note: Preserve the input, output, last complete iteration, code version, parent state, and restart ancestry before changing one cause class at a time.

links.title: The job stops before completion
links.note: Preserve stdout, stderr, scheduler record, exit code, last complete calculation block, and hashes. A stopped job is not itself a numerical or scientific result.
